html:
A conflict in the two English-speaking regions of Cameroon, begun in late 2016 when lawyers and teachers protested the use of French in courts and schools, and turned into a separatist war.

The government of Paul Biya met the protests with arrests, shootings and an internet cut. In October 2017 separatists declared a state they call Ambazonia, and armed groups began fighting the army. Villages were burned by both sides, schools closed for years, and thousands of people were killed and hundreds of thousands fled to the cities and to Nigeria. The roots go back to the 1961 plebiscite and the split of 1916.
sum: A conflict in the two English-speaking regions of Cameroon, begun in late 2016 when lawyers and teachers protested the use of French in courts and schools, and turned into a separatist war.
